strengths: An operating asset that already exists — there is no need to build production capacity from scratch
A quality reputation documented in the local market through word of mouth
The ability to customise to measure — a capability that ready-made stores cannot easily copy

gaps: No digital presence at all: every order arrives on WhatsApp and is logged by hand

market.summary: Egyptian wood furniture is among the largest markets in the region and the least digitally mature: online purchasing of home furniture is still below 5%. Entering with a digital store therefore leads to an existing market rather than a contested share.

porter.evidence: A proliferation of workshops and platforms with no meaningful barriers to entry; the markets are driven by price and service competition.
The cost of digital entry has fallen — a store can be live in two weeks — but the real barrier is delivery capability, not the website.
Most materials are available from more than one supplier, but imports create pressure on a single line.
A customer can collect quotations from five sources in a minute through Facebook groups; price comparison is effortless.
Replacing furniture with cheaper imports, or extending the life of existing pieces instead of buying.

principles: Every agent has a human owner accountable for its output — there is no agent without an owner.
The propose-then-review principle is mandatory for any decision touching money or a customer.
Every agent output is traceable: which data and which instructions produced it.
Customer personal data is never stored outside approved and authorised systems.
A quarterly review of every agent's performance against its defined indicator.
human_in_loop: Any refund or discount above 5% is presented to a human before execution.
Customer service replies that address a complaint or a damage claim are reviewed before sending.
Content published on social media passes human review before it goes live.
Any pricing decision or change to the returns policy is signed off by the Finance Manager.
Closing a customer account or any legal action is never executed automatically.
model_policy: Models are used on non-sensitive data only; sensitive data is processed inside an approved, access-restricted environment.
A weekly review of model performance, documenting any drift in output quality.
No model output may be used without human review in sensitive content.
The version and settings behind every officially approved output are documented.
An approved manual fallback exists for every critical process in case the service is unavailable.
security: Data is encrypted in transit and at rest across every storefront and dashboard path.
Least-privilege access for every agent, reviewed quarterly.
Every action an agent performs is fully logged in an immutable audit trail.
Daily encrypted backups with a monthly restoration test.
A defined incident disclosure and response policy with clear reporting channels.
cost_model: A monthly review of AI tooling subscription cost against the operating benefit it delivers.
Route each task to the cheapest model tier that meets the need — a small model for repetitive work.
The cost per order handled by the assistant is measured against the cost of human handling.
A monthly spend ceiling per agent, with an alert at 80%.

conclusion.summary: The project is financially viable in the base case, but the margin is thin: net present value is positive at only EGP 377,000, and the internal rate of return of 25.6% sits just 1.6 percentage points above the 24% discount rate - a gap that cannot honestly be called a comfortable margin. That finding is itself the most important output of the study, because it changes the nature of the decision: what is being requested is not a single unconditional approval, but a phased approval gated by measurement. The conservative scenario (price 10% lower, sales 25% slower, costs 15% higher) drives net present value to roughly EGP -11.6m and eliminates the internal rate of return altogether; the real risk therefore lies not in the market but in the conversion assumption. What supports the decision is that the operating risk is bounded: the production capacity exists, the workshop is running, and the genuine gap is the digital presence and the data - which is exactly what this transformation closes.
conclusion.recommendation: Approve the first phase with an EGP 8,500,000 budget split between immediate launch capital of EGP 5,700,000, and EGP 2,800,000 for the second CNC router held in escrow conditional upon achieving 70% capacity utilisation for three consecutive months. The 5-year cumulative capital expenditure (5-Year Cumulative CAPEX) totals EGP 10,270,000 (adding EGP 420,000 in Year 1 and EGP 1,350,000 in Year 2). The recommendation is conditional approval reflected in the five governance conditions.
conditions: Pass the 45-day marketing test at a conversion rate of at least 1.4% before releasing the second tranche.
Secure at least two suppliers for every key material before scaled operation begins.
Appoint the digital project manager and the marketing manager within 30 days.
Complete a full security review before connecting the payment gateway.
Do not release the production-line expansion tranche - second CNC router (EGP 2,800,000) held in escrow before current capacity utilisation reaches 70% for three consecutive months.

Launch or defer, based on the test results
Review the feasibility study and update the financial model

do: Start small: 50 carefully selected products rather than an attempt to list everything that can be made.
Document everything from day one — after a furniture workshop, the data is the real asset.
Give the agents specific tasks with clear acceptance criteria rather than a mandate to automate everything.
Review the actual numbers against this study every month, not every quarter.
dont: Do not launch advertising before the product page and checkout are ready — you will waste the acquisition budget.
Do not expand production capacity before current utilisation reaches 70%.
Do not grant the agents broad permissions, however good the early results look.
Do not depend on a single platform as your only acquisition channel.
